questions.question: When you see a disabled pedestrian with a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, should you yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: A disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device has the right-of-way. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian, whether on a sidewalk or roadway.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt at all times. In a crash, an unbuckled person becomes a flying object and can injure everyone in the vehicle.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make gestures to show your disapproval.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if another driver is threatening you. Create distance between your car and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, not what the flagger says.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal road rules as if there were no construction.

questions.explanation: Always slow down and follow directions from flaggers, signs, or police in construction zones. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Retaliate with your own dangerous driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If cut off by an aggressive driver, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to retaliate will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Speed up and drive past them.
Stop and let them cross safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians even when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when a flagger or stop sign tells you to, or when red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.question: Alcohol is the number one cause of fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the leading killer on American roads. It damages vision, slows reaction time, and makes it harder to respond in emergencies. Alcohol affects driving even below the legal limit.

questions.question: You should always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Warns you about road conditions ahead.
Directs you to cities and towns ahead.
Tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to road conditions ahead. They are usually diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. U-turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: Wet roads make it harder to stop and easier to skid. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it hard to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be coming. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: To be safe when crossing a railroad, you should:

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.
Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Listen and look both ways before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving on the roadway and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down and pull over to the right side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: When you see other drivers around you acting or reacting in anger:
questions.explanation: Avoid making eye contact or hand gestures. Stay away from angry drivers. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can to stay safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road hazards ahead. This sign warns drivers that a steep hill is coming. Drivers should slow down to protect their brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: You had a bad experience at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are angry or upset, calm down before you drive. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road. Do not use your car to work out frustration or anger.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and drug may get stronger.
The effects of both the alcohol and drug may get weaker.
Only the alcohol effects may get weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and drug may get stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine could affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slippery roads are especially dangerous on turns and curves. Slow down more than normal when turning on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers. They show where to position your vehicle, mark safe passing areas, and warn drivers about what is ahead.
